products.name: Basics To Advanced In React
products.author: Priya Sharma
products.overview: A complete, project-driven path from React fundamentals to advanced patterns like hooks, context, and performance optimization.
products.long_description: Start with JSX and components, then progress through state management, custom hooks, the Context API, code-splitting, and testing with React Testing Library. Each chapter builds a real feature — a dashboard, a form wizard, an infinite-scroll feed — so you leave with working code, not just theory. Written for developers who already know JavaScript and want a structured, no-fluff route to production-grade React.

products.name: Django Framework for Beginners
products.author: Miguel Torres
products.overview: A hands-on introduction to Django's MTV architecture, ORM, and admin panel — build your first production-ready web app.
products.long_description: Covers project setup, models and migrations, the Django ORM, class-based views, authentication, and deploying to a real server. You'll build a blog engine with user accounts and comments from chapter one, then extend it with REST endpoints using Django REST Framework in the final section. Assumes basic Python knowledge; no prior web framework experience required.

products.name: The Future of Design Systems
products.author: Elena Vogel
products.overview: How component libraries, design tokens, and cross-team governance keep large products visually and functionally consistent.
products.long_description: Explores the practical side of building and maintaining a design system at scale: token architecture, Figma-to-code handoff, versioning components without breaking consumers, and getting engineering and design teams to actually adopt the thing you built. Includes case studies from teams that scaled a design system past 50 contributing engineers.

products.name: The Complete Guide to Backend Development
products.author: David Kim
products.overview: Everything from REST API design and databases to authentication, caching, and horizontal scaling — one comprehensive reference.
products.long_description: A full backend curriculum in one book: relational and NoSQL data modeling, REST and GraphQL API design, JWT and session-based auth, caching strategies with Redis, message queues, rate limiting, and deploying stateless services behind a load balancer. Each part ends with a capstone exercise, culminating in a multi-service backend you build incrementally across the book.

products.name: Build a Blockchain from Scratch in Go
products.author: Anders Lindqvist
products.overview: Implement a working proof-of-work blockchain, wallet, and P2P network in Go — no black boxes, just the code.
products.long_description: Rather than wrapping an existing library, you write every core primitive yourself: block structure, hashing and proof-of-work, a UTXO-based wallet, transaction signing, and a gossip-based P2P network for node discovery. By the end you'll understand exactly what happens under the hood of chains like Bitcoin, using nothing but Go's standard library and a clear, incremental build order.

products.name: Frontend Fastlane Plan With Projects
products.author: Sofia Bianchi
products.overview: Six portfolio-ready projects that take you from static layouts to a fully interactive, API-driven single-page app.
products.long_description: Learn by shipping: a responsive marketing site, an animated dashboard, a drag-and-drop kanban board, a real-time chat UI, an e-commerce cart, and a capstone SPA that ties state management, routing, and API integration together. Each project includes a design file, a starter repo, and a full walkthrough — ideal for building a portfolio while reinforcing modern frontend fundamentals.

products.name: Master the Code Review
products.author: Rachel Okafor
products.overview: The engineering and communication skills that turn code review from a bottleneck into your team's best quality gate.
products.long_description: Covers what to look for beyond syntax — architecture fit, edge cases, security, and maintainability — plus how to give feedback that improves the code without stalling momentum or damaging trust. Includes real annotated pull-request examples, a reviewer's checklist, and guidance for both giving and receiving reviews as a junior or senior engineer.

products.name: JavaScript Basics To Advance With Shubham
products.author: Shubham Rathi
products.overview: A structured JavaScript path from variables and functions through closures, prototypes, async patterns, and the event loop.
products.long_description: Starts with core syntax and data types, then goes deep on the parts developers usually learn the hard way: closures, `this` binding, prototypal inheritance, promises, async/await, and how the event loop actually schedules your code. Every concept is paired with runnable examples and common interview-style problems, making this equally useful as a first JS book or a refresher before technical interviews.

products.name: Python Deep Dive With Projects
products.author: Wei Zhang
products.overview: Move past basic syntax into Python's data model, generators, decorators, and concurrency — reinforced with five real projects.
products.long_description: Digs into what makes Python Python: the data model (dunder methods), iterators and generators, decorators and context managers, and the differences between threading, multiprocessing, and asyncio. Five projects — a CLI tool, a web scraper, a small API, a data pipeline, and an automation script — apply each concept immediately instead of leaving it abstract.

products.name: Mastering Software Technique
products.author: Thomas Neumann
products.overview: Core software design principles — SOLID, composition over inheritance, and clean architecture — explained with real refactors.
products.long_description: Takes intentionally messy, realistic code and refactors it step by step, explaining the reasoning at each stage: extracting responsibilities, favoring composition, decoupling business logic from frameworks, and testing the result. Less about naming design patterns and more about building the judgment to know when applying one actually helps.

products.name: Web Development Foundation
products.author: Isabella Moreau
products.overview: The HTML, CSS, and JavaScript fundamentals every web developer needs before touching a framework.
products.long_description: A ground-up introduction to how the web actually works: semantic HTML, the CSS box model and layout systems (Flexbox and Grid), the DOM, and vanilla JavaScript for interactivity. Deliberately framework-free so you build a solid mental model first — the same one that makes React, Vue, or any framework click faster once you get there.

products.name: Mastering Git and GitHub - A Practical Guide
products.author: Owen Carter
products.overview: From your first commit to resolving gnarly merge conflicts and running a clean team workflow on GitHub.
products.long_description: Covers everyday Git (branching, merging, rebasing, stashing) plus the situations that actually trip people up: interactive rebase, cherry-picking, recovering lost commits with reflog, and untangling merge conflicts with confidence. The second half moves to GitHub specifically — pull request workflows, code owners, protected branches, and Actions basics for CI.

products.name: Everything About React v16
products.author: Priya Sharma
products.overview: A focused reference for React 16's feature set: Fiber, error boundaries, portals, and the early Hooks API.
products.long_description: Documents React 16 in depth — the Fiber reconciler and what it changed under the hood, error boundaries for graceful failure handling, portals for rendering outside the DOM hierarchy, and the Hooks API as it was introduced. Useful as a historical/reference volume for teams maintaining React 16 codebases, or as context for understanding how React's API evolved.

products.name: Diving Deep With Python 2.7
products.author: Wei Zhang
products.overview: A reference for teams still maintaining Python 2.7 codebases — syntax, standard library quirks, and migration notes to Python 3.
products.long_description: Documents Python 2.7's syntax and standard library in detail for engineers supporting legacy systems, with a dedicated final section mapping common Python 2 patterns to their Python 3 equivalents to ease an eventual migration. Not a recommendation to start new projects in Python 2 — a practical reference for the codebases that haven't moved yet.

products.name: Kickstart Your UI Design Career
products.author: Elena Vogel
products.overview: Design fundamentals, portfolio strategy, and the Figma workflow you need to land your first UI design role.
products.long_description: Covers visual design fundamentals (typography, color, spacing, hierarchy), a practical introduction to Figma, and — critically — how to build a portfolio that actually gets interviews. Includes a chapter on presenting design decisions to engineers and stakeholders, since communicating the 'why' behind a design is as important as the design itself when you're starting out.
